Results on comparison and sub/super-stabilizability of some new means

Lenka Mihoković and Mustapha Raïssouli Address: Lenka Mihoković, University of Zagreb, Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computing, Unska 3, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia Email address: lenka.mihokovic@fer.hr Address: Mustapha Raïssouli, Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, Moulay Ismail University, Meknes, Morocco. Email address: raissouli.mustapha@gmail.com
Abstract.

We present analysis of some new means recently introduced by M. Raïssouli and A. Rezgui. We establish comparison relations and results on (K,N)(K,N)-sub/super-stabilizability where KK and NN belong to the class of power means, denoted by BpB_{p}, and MM is one of the classical or recently studied new means. Assuming that means KK, MM and NN have asymptotic expansions, we present the complete asymptotic expansion of the resultant mean-map. As an application of the obtained asymptotic expansions and the asymptotic inequality between MM and ℛ⁡(Bp,M,Bq)\mathcal{R}(B_{p},M,B_{q}), we show how to find the optimal parameters pp and qq for which MM is (Bp,Bq)(B_{p},B_{q})-sub/super-stabilizable.

Key words and phrases: 
Resultant mean-map; Stable mean; Sub-stabilizable mean; Super-stabilizable mean; Asymptotic expansion; Inequalities; Power means
1991 Mathematics Subject Classification
26E60; 41A60; 39B62

1. Introduction

Through this paper we consider bivariate mean, i.e. a function M:ℝ+×ℝ+→ℝ+M\colon\mathbb{R}^{+}\times\mathbb{R}^{+}\to\mathbb{R}^{+} such that min⁡(s,t)≤M⁡(s,t)≤max⁡(s,t).\min(s,t)\leq M(s,t)\leq\max(s,t). We say that mean MM is symmetric if M⁡(s,t)=M⁡(t,s)M(s,t)=M(t,s) for all s,t>0s,t>0, and homogeneous (of degree 1) if M⁡(λ​s,λ​t)=λ​M​(s,t)M(\lambda s,\lambda t)=\lambda M(s,t) for all λ,s,t,>0.\lambda,s,t,>0. For three homogeneous symmetric bivariate means KK, MM and NN, we define the so-called resultant mean-map

ℛ⁡(K,M,N)​(s,t)=K⁡(M⁡(s,N⁡(s,t)),M⁡(N⁡(s,t),t)).\mathcal{R}(K,M,N)(s,t)=K\Bigl(M\bigl(s,N(s,t)\bigr),M\bigl(N(s,t),t\bigr)\Bigr).

A symmetric mean MM is said to be stable (balanced), if ℛ⁡(M,M,M)=M\mathcal{R}(M,M,M)=M.

Definition 1.1 ([9, 11]).

Let KK, NN be two nontrivial stable means. Mean MM is called

  1. (1)

    (K,N)(K,N)-stabilizable, if the following relation is satisfied:

    M⁡(s,t)=ℛ⁡(K,M,N)​(s,t)=K⁡(M⁡(s,N⁡(s,t)),M⁡(N⁡(s,t),t)).M(s,t)=\mathcal{R}(K,M,N)(s,t)=K\Bigl(M\bigl(s,N(s,t)\bigr),M\bigl(N(s,t),t\bigr)\Bigr).
  2. (2)

    (K,N)(K,N)-sub-stabilizable, if ℛ⁡(K,M,N)≤M\mathcal{R}(K,M,N)\leq M and MM is between KK and NN,

  3. (3)

    (K,N)(K,N)-super-stabilizable, if M≤ℛ⁡(K,M,N)M\leq\mathcal{R}(K,M,N) and MM is between KK and NN.

Some interesting results regarding these notions can also be found in papers [1, 12]. Motivated by the results on sub/super-stabilizability for bivariate means studied in the paper [11] in combination with the general algorithms for the coefficients in the asymptotic expansion of the resultant mean-map and consequently of the stabilizable mean, obtained in the paper [8], we present the results on sub/super-stabilizability in the context of the asymptotic expansions.

Definition 1.2.

For an asymptotic sequence of functions (φn)n∈ℕ0(\varphi_{n})_{n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}} the (formal) series ∑n=0∞an​φn​(x)\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_{n}\varphi_{n}(x) is said to be an asymptotic expansion of a function f⁡(x)f(x) as x→x0x\to x_{0} if for each N∈ℕ0N\in\mathbb{N}_{0}

f⁡(x)=∑n=0Nan​φn​(x)+o⁡(φN​(x)).f(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}a_{n}\varphi_{n}(x)+o(\varphi_{N}(x)).

Theoretical background from theory of asymptotic expansions can be found in [7]. Through this paper, we use asymptotic expansion with respect to the asymptotic sequence φn​(x)=x1−n\varphi_{n}(x)=x^{1-n}, n∈ℕ0n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}, as x→∞x\to\infty. Based on the sign of the first term in such asymptotic expansion we introduce the notion of the asymptotic inequality.

Definition 1.3 ([13]).

Let F⁡(s,t)F(s,t) be any homogeneous bivariate function such that

F⁡(x+s,x+t)=ck​(t,s)​x−k+1+𝒪⁡(x−k).F(x+s,x+t)=c_{k}(t,s)x^{-k+1}+{\mathcal{O}}(x^{-k}).

If ck​(s,t)>0c_{k}(s,t)>0 for all ss and tt, then we say FF is asymptotically greater than zero, and write

F≻0.F\succ 0.

Asymptotic inequality is the necessary condition for the proper inequality, i.e. if F≥0F\geq 0, then F≻0F\succ 0.

The subject of study in this paper are means from [10] alone for themselves and also in combinations with power means. Recall the definition of the rr-th power mean

Br​(a,b)={(ar+br2)1/r,r≠0,a​b,r=0.B_{r}(a,b)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\biggl(\frac{a^{r}+b^{r}}{2}\biggr)^{1/r},\qquad&r\neq 0,\\ \sqrt{ab},&r=0.\end{cases}

This class of means covers some well known classical means such as arithmetic mean A=B1A=B_{1}, geometric mean G=B0G=B_{0} and harmonic mean H=B−1H=B_{-1}. It has been proved ([9]) that power means BpB_{p} are stable for all real values of parameter pp. Regarding its asymptotic expansion which has been studied in [6], one may find that

Bp​(x−t,x+t)∼x+12​(p−1)​t2​x−1+124​(p−1)​(3+p−2​p2)​t4​x−3+𝒪⁡(x−5).B_{p}(x-t,x+t)\sim x+\tfrac{1}{2}(p-1)t^{2}x^{-1}+\tfrac{1}{24}(p-1)(3+p-2p^{2})t^{4}x^{-3}+{\mathcal{O}}(x^{-5}). (1.1)
Remark 1.4.

This so-called one variable asymptotic expansion, i.e. asymptotic expansion of a mean in variables (x−t,x+t)(x-t,x+t), is sufficient to determine completely the two variable asymptotic expansion, i.e. asymptotic expansion in variables (x+s,x+t)(x+s,x+t) as it was proved in [2, Lemma 2.1.]. Following the same procedure as in the mentioned Lemma, we may conclude that the first non-zero coefficient in both of those expansions is the same.

mf​(a,b)=2​(a−b)f⁡(ab)−f⁡(ba),a≠b,mf​(a,a)=a.m_{f}(a,b)=\frac{2(a-b)}{f(\frac{a}{b})-f(\frac{b}{a})},\ a\neq b,\qquad m_{f}(a,a)=a.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we establish comparison relations involving means from [10] and some other well-known means. We examine the possibility of being (A,G)(A,G)- or (G,A)(G,A)-sub/super-stabilizable for means defined in (1.3), (1.4) and (1.5). In Section 3, we present complete asymptotic expansions of the above mentioned means. We also extend the result from [8] in order to find the complete asymptotic expansion of the resultant mean-map of means whose asymptotic expansion may include all terms x1−nx^{1-n}, n∈ℕ0n\in\mathbb{N}_{0}, which then could be applied on means which are subject of study in this paper. As a consequence of the coefficient comparison, we find parameters for which means LαL_{\alpha} are stable and disprove the stability for other means. With use of the coefficients in the asymptotic expansion of power means ([6]) we present the coefficients in the asymptotic expansion of the resultant mean-map ℛ⁡(Bp,M,Bq)​(x−t,x+t)\mathcal{R}(B_{p},M,B_{q})(x-t,x+t) as x→∞x\to\infty. In Section 4, we show some of the applications of the obtained results. We analyze the behaviour of the difference M−ℛ⁡(Bp,M,Bq)M-\mathcal{R}(B_{p},M,B_{q}), for each of the means defined in (1.3), (1.4) and (1.5). We examine when each of these means can be (Bp,Bq)(B_{p},B_{q})-sub/super-stabilizable and, when possible, how to find such optimal parameters pp and qq.

2. Comparison of means and sub/super-stabilizability

We start this section by stating some results about comparison between the bivariate means mentioned in the previous section.

Proposition 2.1.

Let α∈[0,1]\alpha\in[0,1]. The following statements hold:

g⁡(x)≔h⁡(x)(1+2​r​x)α+rr−1,g(x)\coloneqq\frac{h(x)}{\big(1+2rx\big)^{\frac{\alpha+r}{r}}-1},

with

h⁡(x)=2​(α+r)​sinh⁡x−(1+2​r​x)α+rr+1.h(x)=2(\alpha+r)\sinh x-\big(1+2rx\big)^{\frac{\alpha+r}{r}}+1.

It is clear that h(x)′=2(r+α)(coshx−(1+2rx)αr)h{{}^{\prime}}(x)=2(r+\alpha)\Big(\cosh x-\big(1+2rx\big)^{\frac{\alpha}{r}}\Big). We have the following situations:

  • •

    If α+r>0\alpha+r>0 then (1+2​r​x)α+rr−1>0\big(1+2rx\big)^{\frac{\alpha+r}{r}}-1>0 and if moreover α≤0\alpha\leq 0 then cosh⁡x>1≥(1+2​r​x)α/r\cosh x>1\geq(1+2rx)^{\alpha/r} for any x>0x>0. In this case, h(x)′>0h{{}^{\prime}}(x)>0 and so h⁡(x)>h⁡(0)=0h(x)>h(0)=0, for all x>0x>0. We then deduce that g⁡(x)>0g(x)>0 for all x>0x>0.

  • •

    If α+r<0\alpha+r<0 then (1+2​r​x)α+rr−1<0\big(1+2rx\big)^{\frac{\alpha+r}{r}}-1<0 and if moreover α≤0\alpha\leq 0 then h(x)′<0h{{}^{\prime}}(x)<0 and so h⁡(x)<h⁡(0)=0h(x)<h(0)=0, for all x>0x>0. We then infer that g⁡(x)>0g(x)>0 for any x>0x>0.

Summarizing, we have shown the desired result.

The inequality Mα,r<AM_{\alpha,r}<A, for α≥0\alpha\geq 0, can be established in a similar way, and we leave it to the reader. ∎

Remark 2.5.

Numerical computations show that, if α>0\alpha>0 (resp. α<0\alpha<0) then Mα,rM_{\alpha,r} is not comparable with GG (resp. AA).

We will now study the sub/super-stabilizability of some of the above means. We recall the following result.

Proposition 2.6 ([11]).

Let MM be a continuous symmetric mean. Then

  1. (i)

    If MM is (A,G)(A,G)-sub-stabilizable then L≤M≤AL\leq M\leq A.

  2. (ii)

    If MM is (A,G)(A,G)-super-stabilizable then G≤M≤LG\leq M\leq L.

Combining Proposition 2.6 with Proposition 2.1 and Proposition 2.3 we immediately deduce the following corollary.

Corollary 2.7.

Let α∈[0,1]\alpha\in[0,1]. The following statements hold:

  1. (i)

    LαL_{\alpha} is not (A,G)(A,G)-sub-stabilizable and SαS_{\alpha} is not (A,G)(A,G)-super-stabilizable.

  2. (ii)

    If 1/2<α≤11/2<\alpha\leq 1 then LαL_{\alpha} is not (A,G)(A,G)-super-stabilizable.

  3. (iii)

    The three means M1,M3M_{1},M_{3} and M5M_{5} are neither (A,G)(A,G)-sub/super-stabilizable nor (G,A)(G,A)-sub/super-stabilizable.

To giving more results about sub/super-stabilizability we need the following lemma.

Lemma 2.8 ([9]).

Let mm be a symmetric homogeneous mean. Then, for any a,b>0a,b>0, we have

ℛ⁡(A,m,G)​(a,b)=A⁡(a,b)​m​(a,b).\mathcal{R}(A,m,G)(a,b)=A\big(\sqrt{a},\sqrt{b}\big)\;m\big(\sqrt{a},\sqrt{b}\big).

Now, we may state the following result.

Theorem 2.9.

Let 0<α≤2/20<\alpha\leq\sqrt{2}/2. Then, SαS_{\alpha} is strictly (A,G)(A,G)-sub-stabilizable. In particular, the first Seiffert mean P=S1/2P=S_{1/2} is strictly (A,G)(A,G)-sub-stabilizable.

Proof.

Firstly, by following Proposition 2.1 we have G≤Sα≤AG\leq S_{\alpha}\leq A for any 0<α≤2/20<\alpha\leq\sqrt{2}/2. According to Definition 1.1 we have to prove that the inequality ℛ⁡(A,Sα,G)​(a,b)<Sα​(a,b)\mathcal{R}\big(A,S_{\alpha},G\big)(a,b)<S_{\alpha}(a,b) holds for any a>ba>b. By Lemma 2.8, with substitution (1.6), it is equivalent to show that the inequality

fA​(x2)​fSα​(x2)<fSα​(x)f_{A}(\tfrac{x}{2})f_{S_{\alpha}}(\tfrac{x}{2})<f_{S_{\alpha}}(x)

holds for any x>0x>0, and in combination with the corresponding relations in (1.8) and in (1.9), this is equivalent to

α​cosh⁡(x/2)​sinh⁡(x/2)arctan⁡(tanh⁡(α​x/2))<α​sinh⁡xarctan⁡(tanh⁡(α​x)),\alpha\cosh(x/2)\frac{\sinh(x/2)}{\arctan\big(\tanh(\alpha x/2)\big)}<\alpha\frac{\sinh x}{\arctan\big(\tanh(\alpha x)\big)},

for x>0x>0. Using formula sinh⁡x=2​sinh⁡(x/2)​cosh⁡(x/2)\sinh x=2\sinh(x/2)\cosh(x/2) and setting g⁡(x)≔arctan⁡(tanh⁡(α​x))−2​arctan⁡(tanh⁡(α​x/2))g(x)\coloneqq\arctan\big(\tanh(\alpha x)\big)-2\arctan\big(\tanh(\alpha x/2)\big) we easily verify that g(x)′<0g{{}^{\prime}}(x)<0 and so g⁡(x)<g⁡(0)=0g(x)<g(0)=0, for all x>0x>0. We then deduce the desired result. ∎

Theorem 2.10.

Let 0<α<1/20<\alpha<1/2. Then LαL_{\alpha} is strictly (A,G)(A,G)-super-stabilizable. In particular, the Heinz mean H​Z1/4=L1/4HZ_{1/4}=L_{1/4} is strictly (A,G)(A,G)-super-stabilizable.

Proof.

By similar way and similar arguments as in the proof of the previous theorem, we are here reduced to study the sign of g⁡(x)≔sinh⁡(2​α​x)−2​sinh⁡(α​x)g(x)\coloneqq\sinh(2\alpha x)-2\sinh(\alpha x) for x>0x>0. Obviously, g(x)′≔2αcosh(2αx)−2αcosh(αx)>0g{{}^{\prime}}(x)\coloneqq 2\alpha\cosh(2\alpha x)-2\alpha\cosh(\alpha x)>0 and so g⁡(x)>g⁡(0)=0g(x)>g(0)=0, for any x>0x>0 so concluding the proof. ∎

Theorem 2.11.

The means M2M_{2} and M4M_{4} are both strictly (A,G)(A,G)-sub-stabilizable.

Proof.

It is also similar to the previous proofs. The details are straightforward and therefore omitted here. ∎

4. Sub-stabilizability and super-stabilizability with power means

In this Section we present some of the possible applications of the previously obtained results. We will show the use of asymptotic expansions when examining the possibility for a given mean to be (Bp,Bq)(B_{p},B_{q})-sub- or super-stabilizable and when possible, how to find optimal parameters pp and qq.

Since the asymptotic inequality is the necessary condition for the proper inequality, we analyse when

M−ℛ⁡(Bp,M,Bq)≻0.M-\mathcal{R}(B_{p},M,B_{q})\succ 0. (4.1)

The best approximation is obtained when as many as possible first coefficients are equal to 0. See [13] for detailed analysis. Because of the reasoning in Remark 1.4, it is sufficient to use the expansions in variables (x−t,x+t)(x-t,x+t).

Asymptotic inequality corresponds the proper inequality for means when variables ss and tt are close enough to each other. In order to complement the information obtained form asymptotic side, it is often useful to observe relation between means about the point (0,1)(0,1). For more details we refer to paper [4].

Example 4.1.

Let M=LαM=L_{\alpha}. Observe the difference between (3.1) and (3.8). When equating the coefficient by x−1x^{-1} with 0, we have that q=12​(1−p)−2​α2q=\frac{1}{2}(1-p)-2\alpha^{2} and then

and if also p=±1+16​α2−16​α4p=\pm\sqrt{1+16\alpha^{2}-16\alpha^{4}} then

Hence, for such pp and qq, (4.1) holds for 12<|α|<1\frac{1}{2}<\lvert{\alpha}\rvert<1, and we have the opposite inequality sign in (4.1) for 0<|α|<120<\lvert{\alpha}\rvert<\frac{1}{2}.

Additionally, when we equate coefficient by x−5x^{-5} with 0, we obtain the following trivial (and already known) cases: α=±12,q=−p\alpha=\pm\frac{1}{2},q=-p; α=0,p=−1,q=1\alpha=0,p=-1,q=1; α=0,p=1,q=0\alpha=0,p=1,q=0; α=±1,p=1,q=−2\alpha=\pm 1,p=1,q=-2; where the stabilizability is achieved.

On the other side, values of limits lims→0Lα​(s,1−s)=0\lim_{s\to 0}L_{\alpha}(s,1-s)=0 and lims→0ℛ⁡(Bp,Lα,Bq)​(s,1−s)>0\lim_{s\to 0}\mathcal{R}(B_{p},L_{\alpha},B_{q})(s,1-s)>0 for any pp and qq, imply that LαL_{\alpha} could only be (Bp,Bq)(B_{p},B_{q})-super-stabilizable.
